evals.name: project-system-leads
evals.prompt: Our repo has a design-tokens.json with brand colors and a DESIGN.md that says errors are shown in a red banner with an icon. Design the error state for the new upload form.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs detect, finds the project's token file and design doc, and designs the error state from them: the red banner and icon the project already uses, colors from design-tokens.json. It names what it found and does not introduce a new error style or offer a style-imposing tool for a concern the project already defines.
expectations: The response names the project's own design-tokens.json and DESIGN.md as what decides the error state
The error state uses the banner-with-icon pattern the project already defines rather than a new style
The response does not offer frontend-design, design-taste-frontend or ui-ux-pro-max for this concern

evals.name: cli-output-terminal-rules
evals.prompt: Design the output for my CLI's `sync` command: progress while it runs and a summary at the end. People run it in CI too.
evals.expected_output: The skill states the target platforms before designing (Windows, macOS, Linux and WSL when unstated), designs progress for an interactive terminal, and gives the non-TTY behavior for CI: no color, spinner or cursor movement, plain parseable lines. It honors NO_COLOR and gives a plain-ASCII fallback.
expectations: The response names the operating systems, shells or terminals the output must work in before or while designing it
The response says that when output is not a TTY (as in CI) it emits no color, spinner, cursor movement or animation
The response says NO_COLOR set to any non-empty value turns color off
The response gives a plain-ASCII fallback for dumb terminals or missing Nerd Font glyphs

evals.name: routes-to-installed-tool
evals.prompt: Build me a landing page hero section. I have the frontend-design plugin from claude-plugins-official installed and enabled, and this project has no design system yet.
evals.expected_output: With no project design system and frontend-design installed, the skill routes the visual-direction concern to frontend-design by its exact id and says why, rather than answering only from its own guidance. It may offer to create a small token file for the gap, and creates nothing without the user's agreement.
expectations: The response routes the visual direction to frontend-design and says why it chose that route
The response does not create a token or design-system file without asking first

evals.name: nothing-installed-own-guidance
evals.prompt: How should my TUI's status bar look? I don't have any design plugins installed.
evals.expected_output: With nothing installed for the concern, the skill answers from its own terminal guidance (theme-safe named ANSI colors, display width in columns, plain fallback) and may name a free tool that would help, without installing anything.
expectations: The response answers from the plugin's own terminal guidance rather than claiming a route to an installed tool
The response uses the terminal's named ANSI colors rather than fixed 24-bit values, or says to
The response installs nothing and asks before any install it suggests

evals.name: layout-variants-hand-off
evals.prompt: Give me three throwaway layout variants of our settings page that I can flip between in the browser.
evals.expected_output: Throwaway layout variants are /prototype:explore-directions's job. The skill points the user there (its Next section) instead of building a variant switcher itself.
expectations: The response points to /prototype:explore-directions for throwaway layout variants

evals.name: animation-build-routes-to-authoring
evals.prompt: Our design is settled. Now add an entrance animation to the onboarding cards.
evals.expected_output: Building an interface animation is the animation-authoring concern. The skill routes to its highest-ranked installed route, this plugin’s /user-interface:write-animation when nothing ranked above it applies, and says which route it took.
expectations: The response routes the request to the animation-authoring concern or to /user-interface:write-animation
The response says which route it took

evals.name: animation-review-routes-to-audit
evals.prompt: Can you check whether the animations we added in this branch are any good?
evals.expected_output: Reviewing existing animation is the animation-audit concern, whose first route is /user-interface:audit; the skill routes there instead of reviewing the motion itself.
expectations: The response routes the review to /user-interface:audit or the animation-audit concern

evals.name: touch-web-guidance-read
evals.prompt: Design the mobile web version of our signup form. Most people fill it in on their phones.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads web.md and, because the form is used by touch on phones, touch-web.md; the answer applies touch guidance such as press feedback without hover dependence, target sizes that meet the WCAG target size criterion, the right on-screen keyboard per field, no zoom lock, and safe viewport sizing.
expectations: The answer reads or cites touch-web.md or applies at least three of its rules (hover gating, target size, input keyboard, no zoom lock, viewport units)
The answer does not lock zoom

evals.name: installed-component-library-kept
evals.prompt: We need a date picker for the booking form. Our app already uses a headless component library for its dialogs and menus. What should we use?
evals.expected_output: With nothing routed for the concern, the skill answers from component-libraries.md: it prefers the library the project already uses (or a picker built on the same primitives) and does not churn the installed dependency, choosing on accessibility, stack fit, maintenance and license.
expectations: The answer prefers the component library already in the project, or explains why it cannot cover a date picker
The answer does not propose replacing the installed library

evals.name: team-deny-names-team-file
evals.prompt: Build me a landing page hero section. I have the frontend-design plugin from claude-plugins-official installed and enabled, and this project has no design system yet. Our team's settings are in docs/conventions/user-interface.yaml.
evals.expected_output: With the fixture at docs/conventions/user-interface.yaml, detect.mjs lists the frontend-design rows in `skipped` with by `deny`, name frontend-design and source docs/conventions/user-interface.yaml. frontend-design is a confirmed, installed route for visual direction, so Step 4 would have considered it: the answer says the team file denied it, names that file as the source of the skip, and does not route the visual direction to frontend-design.
expectations: The answer says the frontend-design route was skipped because the team routing denies it
The answer names docs/conventions/user-interface.yaml, the team file, as the source of the skip
The answer does not route the visual direction to frontend-design

evals.name: offer-confirmed-uninstalled-route
evals.prompt: Turn our settings screen into an editable design file my designer can open in a design tool. I don't have any design tools or MCP servers installed. Our team's settings are in docs/conventions/user-interface.yaml.
evals.expected_output: The fixture marks the pencil row of the design-tool-handoff concern confirmed; every other row for that concern stays deferred and nothing is installed. The skill offers Pencil as the better route: it names the tool, points to the row's pointer (https://docs.pen.dev/getting-started/installation) for the install command and the sign-in step its login account needs, says to install at local scope, and asks before installing. It states no install command of its own and runs nothing from the pointer page before a yes. It offers no deferred row such as figma, installs nothing, and meanwhile answers from its own guidance.
expectations: The answer offers Pencil for the handoff and asks whether to install it
The answer points to https://docs.pen.dev/getting-started/installation for the install and sign-in steps rather than stating an install command of its own
The answer offers no tool other than Pencil for the handoff: the figma@claude-plugins-official, canva@claude-plugins-official, sketch and penpot rows stay deferred in the merged routes
The answer installs nothing and runs no install command

evals.name: offer-declined-continues
evals.prompt: Turn our settings screen into an editable design file my designer can open in a design tool. I don't have any design tools or MCP servers installed. If you'd suggest installing Pencil or any other design tool, my answer is no, I don't want to install anything. Our team's settings are in docs/conventions/user-interface.yaml.
evals.expected_output: With the fixture's confirmed pencil row and the user's no to installing Pencil, the skill installs nothing and continues with the best present route: for design-tool-handoff nothing is installed, so it answers from its own guidance (for example a structured spec of the screen the designer can rebuild from). It does not ask again whether to install Pencil.
expectations: The answer installs nothing and runs no install command
The answer continues with the design work from the best present route or the plugin's own guidance rather than stopping
The answer does not ask again whether to install Pencil

evals.name: offer-accepted-installs-local
evals.prompt: Turn our settings screen into an editable design file my designer can open in a design tool. I don't have any design tools or MCP servers installed. If you'd suggest installing Pencil, yes, install it. Our team's settings are in docs/conventions/user-interface.yaml.
evals.expected_output: With the fixture's confirmed pencil row and the user's yes to Pencil, the skill reads the row's pointer (https://docs.pen.dev/getting-started/installation) as data for this platform's install and sign-in steps, shows the user the exact command that installs Pencil at local scope with that URL as its source, and asks for a yes to that command before running it: the yes in the prompt covers the tool, not a command the user has not seen. It reports anything else the page says to run, download or edit instead of running it. After the user's yes to the command it runs only that command, runs detect again, and routes the handoff to Pencil once Step 4 picks it; when its reachable is null or false it tells the user to finish signing in.
expectations: The answer takes its install and sign-in steps from https://docs.pen.dev/getting-started/installation
The answer installs at local scope, not user or project scope
The answer shows the user the exact command that installs Pencil and asks for a yes to that command before running it, rather than running it on the yes to the tool alone
The answer runs no command other than the one that installs Pencil, reporting any other download, server or config or shell profile edit the page asks for instead of running it
The answer gives the user Pencil's sign-in step, from the pointer

evals.name: motion-request-reads-every-matching-spoke
evals.prompt: Design the motion for our mobile web bottom sheet: it slides up when opened, people swipe it down to dismiss, and on low-end Android phones it drops frames while it moves.
evals.expected_output: The request matches the motion concern, and the read_when of all four of its spokes holds: catalog.md always, behaviors.md for the drawer or sheet, gestures.md for the swipe, and performance.md for the dropped frames. The skill reads all four in this pass and the design uses each: the drawer curve and a duration within the large limit from the catalog, the sheet's open and close behavior, dismissal on a release faster than a velocity threshold set higher than a small element's and tuned on a device, with the release velocity handed to a spring, and transform and opacity only, checked against the frame budget on a device.
expectations: The answer uses the drawer easing curve and a duration within the large limit for opening and closing the sheet
The answer dismisses on a fast release past a velocity threshold, not on drag distance alone, and carries the release velocity into the settle
The answer animates only transform and opacity, or says layout properties cause the dropped frames
The answer covers all three parts the request names (opening, swipe to dismiss and dropped frames) in this pass rather than leaving one for a later pass
